Installation view from Hilma af Klint – The Ten Largest, 2022 © Stiftelsen Hilma af Klints Verk. Photo: Åsa Lundén / Moderna Museet

# Hilma af Klint
## About the exhibition
It was autumn 1907 when the Swedish artist Hilma af Klint (1862–1944) began the first canvas in a series that would come to be known as “The Ten Largest”. Working on these ten paintings over a period of just 40 days, the result she produced is one of the most monumental legacies of her artistic output. The series is part of a larger collection known as “Paintings for the Temple”, a mammoth project that the artist had embarked upon two years earlier after experiencing non-verbal cues from the spirit world. The challenge of understanding these messages and finding a visual expression for an invisible reality was to preoccupy Hilma af Klint throughout the rest of her life.
Throughout her life, Hilma af Klint sought the right context for her paintings and only showed them to a limited number of people while waiting for the world to become ready to receive their message. Today, more than a hundred years later, her work is acclaimed all over the world.
Hilma af Klint, De tio största, nr 10, Ålderdomen, grupp IV, 1907 © Stiftelsen Hilma af Klints Verk. Photo: Albin Dahlström / Moderna Museet

# Hilma af Klint
## About the exhibition
### Evolution and spirit worlds
The sheer size of “The Ten Largest” sets them apart from the artist’s other works. In a gigantic 3.28×2.40 metre format, Hilma af Klint celebrates the four ages of humanity: Childhood, Youth, Adulthood and Old Age.
A central theme in “The Ten Largest”, as in the artist’s oeuvre as a whole, is the notion of evolution. Hilma af Klint, however, seems less concerned about evolution in terms of any physical development from one form of existence to another, and focuses instead on evolution on a spiritual plane.
This reflects an interest in spirituality and theosophy that she shared with many of her contemporaries.

# Hilma af Klint
## About the exhibition
### Close collaboration with The Hilma af Klint Foundation
Thanks to the close collaboration between Moderna Museet and The Hilma af Klint Foundation, in autumn 2022 visitors to the Museum can renew their acquaintance with “The Ten Largest” by Hilma af Klint, showing in Stockholm for the first time since 2013.
The exhibition also includes a selection of watercolours and a collection of hand-coloured photographs that has never previously been on public display in its entirety.

# Hilma af Klint
The Ten Largest
22.9 2022–8.1 2023
Stockholm
Meet Hilma af Klint and her series of paintings “The Ten Largest”, when the works are once again on show in the museum in autumn 2022. This time the paintings will be exhibited together with a selection of the artist’s watercolours and a complete collection of hand-coloured photographs of “The Ten Largest” that has never previously been shown in its entirety.

Installation view from Hilma af Klint – The Ten Largest, 2022 © Stiftelsen Hilma af Klints Verk. Photo: Åsa Lundén / Moderna Museet
texts.4:
# Hilma af Klint
## About the exhibition
It was autumn 1907 when the Swedish artist Hilma af Klint (1862–1944) began the first canvas in a series that would come to be known as “The Ten Largest”. Working on these ten paintings over a period of just 40 days, the result she produced is one of the most monumental legacies of her artistic output. The series is part of a larger collection known as “Paintings for the Temple”, a mammoth project that the artist had embarked upon two years earlier after experiencing non-verbal cues from the spirit world. The challenge of understanding these messages and finding a visual expression for an invisible reality was to preoccupy Hilma af Klint throughout the rest of her life.
Throughout her life, Hilma af Klint sought the right context for her paintings and only showed them to a limited number of people while waiting for the world to become ready to receive their message. Today, more than a hundred years later, her work is acclaimed all over the world.
Hilma af Klint, De tio största, nr 10, Ålderdomen, grupp IV, 1907 © Stiftelsen Hilma af Klints Verk. Photo: Albin Dahlström / Moderna Museet
texts.5:
# Hilma af Klint
## About the exhibition
### Evolution and spirit worlds
The sheer size of “The Ten Largest” sets them apart from the artist’s other works. In a gigantic 3.28×2.40 metre format, Hilma af Klint celebrates the four ages of humanity: Childhood, Youth, Adulthood and Old Age.
A central theme in “The Ten Largest”, as in the artist’s oeuvre as a whole, is the notion of evolution. Hilma af Klint, however, seems less concerned about evolution in terms of any physical development from one form of existence to another, and focuses instead on evolution on a spiritual plane.
This reflects an interest in spirituality and theosophy that she shared with many of her contemporaries.
texts.6:
# Hilma af Klint
## About the exhibition
### Close collaboration with The Hilma af Klint Foundation
Thanks to the close collaboration between Moderna Museet and The Hilma af Klint Foundation, in autumn 2022 visitors to the Museum can renew their acquaintance with “The Ten Largest” by Hilma af Klint, showing in Stockholm for the first time since 2013.
The exhibition also includes a selection of watercolours and a collection of hand-coloured photographs that has never previously been on public display in its entirety.

[[](https://www.instagram.com/pomo_trondheim) pomo_trondheim 7,259 🔥 Ta med venner, kjæresten eller kom alene – på tekstilverksted 18. mars kl.19:30 på PoMo! 🔥 Vi fresher opp gamle klær, tar et glass og lar praten og kreativiteten flyte. Ta med egne tekstiler eller kjøp hos oss – vi fikser resten. 💎 Lyst til å lage din egen notatbok eller et fotoalbum med skikkelig personlig preg? Eller kanskje trykke tekst på tekstil, brodere, sy eller gå all in med «rhinestones»? Vi viser deg hvordan. 🎉 Tekstilverkstedet er en del av PoMo Projects – en arrangementsrekke for unge voksne som vil være sosiale, kreative og prøve noe nytt. 18-årsgrense, baren er åpen og stemningen er god. 👩‍🎨 Verkstedet er inspirert av kunstneren Louise Bourgeois’ lange arbeid med tekstil – et materiale hun brukte for å utforske blant annet minner og identitet. Vi låner litt av hennes utforskende tilnærming og lar tekstil bli et rom for kreativt arbeid. 🚨 Billetten gir inngang til museet hele dagen. Les mer og kjøp billetter på pomo.no Alle verker: Louise Bourgeois © The Easton Foundation/VAGA at ARS/BONO, Oslo 2026 +++++ 🔥 Bring your friends, your partner or come alone – to the fabric workshop on 18th March at 19:30 at PoMo! 🔥 We freshen up old clothes, have a drink and let the conversation and creativity flow. Bring your own textiles or buy from us – we’ll do the rest. 💎 Want to make your own notebook or photo album with a really personal touch? Or maybe print text on textiles, embroider, sew or go all in with “rhinestones”? We’ll show you how. 🎉 The textile workshop is part of PoMo Projects – a series of events for young adults who want to be social, creative and try something new. Age limit 18+, the bar is open and the atmosphere is good.

[[](https://www.instagram.com/kbh_kunst) kbh_kunst 3,704 Kunstner portræt/artist portrait Oana Tudose (b. 1987, Romania) is a visual artist and designer based in Denmark. Her work is grounded in sustained material engagement with textile traditions shaped by repair, reuse, and scarcity. Drawing from Eastern European cultural contexts, intergenerational knowledge, and personal memory, she examines care, vulnerability, and repair as forms of ethical labor developed through endurance, maintenance, and responsibility. Her work has been presented internationally in Denmark, Romania, and the Netherlands, including solo exhibitions at MNTRplusC, Bucharest; Museum of Oradea; and exhibitions in Copenhagen. Her work is held in the Museum of Oradea collection and in private collections across Europe #gallerikbhkunst #kunsttilvæggen #artisttalk #tekstilkunst #fineart @oana_tudose_](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DWlPrrlI79z/?utm_source=popular_topic_grid)
